documentation.description: Estimate the recall and cost of approximate kNN search configurations against a more thorough baseline configuration. Each candidate reports recall of the baseline top-k (not of relevance judgments) plus a recall_stats distribution of the per-query values, which is quantized to multiples of 1/k, and a recall_histogram, which reports every distinct observed value for k up to 20 and otherwise bins them: when recall_histogram_bin_width (0.05) is present each recall is the lower edge of a half-open bin [recall, recall + width), except 1.0 which is exact. All configurations run against a single point-in-time; the baseline runs first, so reported took_ms reflects an index it has already warmed while vector_ops does not.

index.description: A comma-separated list of index names to search

ignore_unavailable.description: Whether specified concrete indices should be ignored when unavailable (missing or closed)

allow_no_indices.description: Whether to allow (1) wildcard index expressions that match no indices and (2) requests where the final resolved set is empty.

expand_wildcards.description: Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both.

body.description: The kNN evaluation definition, including the vector field, k, the query set, an optional filter, the batch and concurrency limits, and the baseline and candidate search configurations (visit_percentage, num_candidates, oversample; a baseline oversample of about 10 makes the reference effectively exact, since the mapping default of 3 rescores too small a window). The baseline may be omitted, in which case it defaults to exact:true. An exact baseline brute-forces every document for a certification run and requires search.allow_expensive_queries; that costs O(N x dims x 4 bytes) per query, so use a small sample.size, and its baseline_vector_ops are float32 comparisons over every live vector (baseline_vector_ops_kind: full_precision_scan) rather than the mostly 1-bit comparisons plus rescore window an approximate baseline reports (quantized_visit_plus_rescore) - comparable as work done, not as bytes. Every non-exact knob set is echoed with rescore_window and effective_num_candidates, both capped at 10000 (so oversample saturates at 10000/k); these need view_index_metadata and are omitted without it.
